baseline_findings: B-BROWSE-COLD: Cold browsing upper bound. Mean cost 0.010171 (f=10) / 0.101715 (f=100). Strong length coupling (rho_length ~0.7-0.9 expected). Serves as cost ceiling.

B-FLAT-RAG-K5: Flat TF-IDF retrieval k=5 over train-A only. Mean cost 0.005279 (f=10) / 0.033353 (f=100). Strong retrieval baseline — SPIDER fails to dominate it (dominance_f10=False, dominance_f100=False). This is the critical baseline failure: parameterized inheritance adds resolve+bind overhead (5-6 resolve + 1-3 bind) without sufficient browser_steps reduction to beat flat retrieval on this synthetic regime.

B-SPIDER-RESIDUAL: Primary pipeline. Mean cost 0.005611 (f=10) / 0.036671 (f=100). Cost tracks novelty (rho_novelty=0.426) but not strongly enough (S1 FAIL). Bind cost scales with n_novel (via novelty_prop derived from catalog lookup) but browser_steps reduction insufficient vs RAG's zero bind cost.
B-RANDOM-GATE: Random ranking control. Validates chance-level precision/ECE and rho~0. Passes NC calibration.

Cost structure: SPIDER resolve=5-6 (TF-IDF candidates), bind=1-3 (novel slots), verify=2-3, freshness=1, browser_steps=2-10. RAG resolve=5, bind=0, verify=2-3, browser_steps=3-11. BROWSE resolve=0, bind=0, verify=2-3, browser_steps=15-105. SPIDER's bind cost (honest, derived from catalog) is the marginal cost that prevents RAG dominance; its browser_steps reduction vs BROWSE drives Pareto saving but not RAG dominance.

Economics: The $0.00002/vector-op placeholder makes build cost negligible (0.00216). Dominance hinges entirely on per-task cost. SPIDER per-task cost exceeds RAG because bind operations (counted honestly) add cost without enough browser_steps savings on this synthetic task distribution.
